chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: Savannah Churchill and Baby Lawrence at the Regal in Chicago
summary: Jones tells how the band, short of a woman on a theater bill, bought Savannah Churchill two dresses to sing "St. Louis Blues" and added dancer Baby Lawrence.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When did you leave? That's as long as you were there.
No, I was there.
But when did you leave?
I didn't go in the Army till '44, but you see in the meantime between Thelma and whatever vocalist they had -
Was Rushing there all through this?

Rushing was still there, straight ahead. We're going on. Now when we get in Chicago we don't have no one woman, so that's where Savannah Churchill came in to sing just "St. Louis Blues" and Ken Bluett went down on 63rd Street and bought her a dress to just sing "St. Louis Blues" which she could sing out of meter but she looked good. Now we got 9 men on the show and no women. Now you can't do that with people standing in lines. You got 7,000 people in a theatre, you got to have a woman up there. That's when we went up to Joe Hughes and got Baby Lawrence with sneakers on to come out and dance. They said, "He's
JONES 190
a singer." I said, "He can dance."
Joe Hughes has a night club on 63rd and South Parkway which is now Martin Luther King Drive.
Ken Bluett and I went down on 63rd Street and bought this Savannah Churchill two dresses.
Where were you playing then?
The Regal.
You were playing the Regal Theatre with Savannah Churchill...
We didn't have a woman -
When did you say that was, approximately?

Around about '43. Bennie Carter had his band and Bennie took Savannah Churchill to put in his band because she only did the week. She looked good and the War was on and she was like Lena Horne - when she walked out on the stage it was fabulous.
She was a beautiful woman.

We only had "St. Louis Blues" for her to sing. She was out of meter but we'd follow her, but she looked good. She had this white gown and another gown - there were only two dresses. Ken Bluett bought it. He was the manager of the Regal. I went with him and got in his car to get this thing and I went up and got Baby Lawrence and when I come in Dickie Wells said, "Man, he's a singer. He was with Don Redman when he was 14." I said, "Yeh, but he can dance."
JONES 191
So we made a little thing and we got Baby Lawrence. That's how it started.
That was the show?
That was the show. Mr. Benny Carter came in with his band - he had a band -
The Regal Theatre?
